narrativeReportMd:
# DocumentManifest R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`DocumentManifest` is a hard breaking removal in the R6 ballot package. R4 instances with `resourceType: "DocumentManifest"` have no R6 core StructureDefinition to validate against, and generated R6 model/API surfaces should not be expected to include a DocumentManifest class, endpoint, or resource-type enum value.

## Scope
I compared the R4 `DocumentManifest` StructureDefinition with the R6 ballot core package. The R6 StructureDefinition and package-index entry are absent; the only direct R6 mention found in core artifacts is the `fhir-old-types` CodeSystem marker. Base `DomainResource`/`Element` constraints and detailed reports for possible replacement resources are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The main issue is not an individual cardinality or binding tweak: the resource is gone. Existing data, REST routes, search clients, validators, generated classes, and references to `DocumentManifest/...` need a migration policy. There is no computable one-to-one replacement in the inspected inputs; `List`, `DocumentReference`, `Composition`, and `Bundle` each cover only part of the R4 manifest use case.

## Highest-impact findings
- `DocumentManifest:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:removed-r6`: the core resource definition is absent in R6, which is a direct R4-to-R6 validation break.
- `DocumentManifest:CONVERSION_OR_MAPPING:DocumentManifest.content:no-direct-r6-model`: manifest grouping and metadata require profile-specific migration decisions rather than a lossless mechanical rename.

## Findings requiring human review
The removal itself is high-confidence. Human review is needed for migration design because the inspected R6 ballot artifacts do not publish an official ConceptMap/StructureMap or narrative replacement guidance.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive path would have been to keep `DocumentManifest` as a deprecated resource for one release or publish an official cross-version mapping. The R4 resource was trial-use/FMM 2, which may explain why removal was considered acceptable, but it does not reduce the break for existing systems.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `List`, `DocumentReference`, `Composition`, and `Bundle` reports before choosing a target model. Also check implementation guides and local profiles that may have constrained R4 `DocumentManifest` enough to allow a deterministic migration.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `DocumentManifest` is removed from the R6 ballot core package. The top migration concerns are invalid R4 instances, removed generated/API surfaces, and lack of an official one-to-one replacement. The main uncertainty is the intended replacement strategy, not the fact of removal.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should start by classifying how each R4 `DocumentManifest` was used: XDS-style manifests of `DocumentReference` resources, general resource groupings, EN 13606 extracts, or workflow-related collections. Candidate R6 targets differ by use case: `List` can group resource references, `DocumentReference` describes a document, and `Composition` plus `Bundle` models FHIR documents. None preserves every R4 field and semantic expectation without policy choices or extensions.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the resource is removed: the expected R6 StructureDefinition is absent, the R6 package index has no entry, `fhir-types` does not include `DocumentManifest`, and `fhir-old-types` explicitly lists it as an old type. Confidence is medium for migration advice because no official diff, narrative rationale, ConceptMap, or StructureMap was available in the local inputs.

findings.title: DocumentManifest resource is absent from the R6 core package

oldState.summary: R4 defines DocumentManifest as a concrete DomainResource resource.

semanticText.short: A list that defines a set of documents
semanticText.definition: A collection of documents compiled for a purpose together with metadata that applies to the collection.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `DocumentManifest` is a real resource type with local elements including required `status` and required repeating `content`. It can appear as a top-level FHIR resource with `resourceType: "DocumentManifest"`.

newState.summary: No R6 StructureDefinition or package-index entry exists for DocumentManifest.

semanticText.definition: R6 `fhir-old-types` lists DocumentManifest as an old resource name no longer used in this version of FHIR.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 ballot package does not contain `StructureDefinition-DocumentManifest.json`, and `.index.json` has no `DocumentManifest` StructureDefinition. The old resource name survives only as an old-type terminology marker, not as a valid resource definition.

facts.note: This supports intentional removal or rename, but does not define a usable R6 resource.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and expected new artifact were matched by canonical resource name and StructureDefinition path. No R6 artifact with the same canonical type exists, and local searches found no direct replacement StructureDefinition; therefore this is classified as removal rather than a same-artifact element change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break. An R4 instance whose top-level `resourceType` is `DocumentManifest` has no R6 core StructureDefinition and will be rejected by strict R6 validators, parsers, JSON/XML schema pipelines, generated model binders, and REST implementations that enumerate allowed R6 resource types. Runtime code that calls `[base]/DocumentManifest`, switches on a `DocumentManifest` resource enum, or validates references such as `DocumentManifest/123` also needs redesign.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The clinical/business risk depends on whether an implementation used DocumentManifest for document sharing or workflow packaging. Where it was used to organize clinical documents, loss of the manifest can affect discoverability, routing, and auditability unless a replacement pattern is chosen.

justification.inferredGoal: Retire a trial-use/FMM 2 document-manifest resource from the core model and direct implementations toward other document or collection patterns.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain DocumentManifest in R6 core as a deprecated compatibility resource while steering new implementations to List, DocumentReference, Composition, or Bundle patterns.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R4 `DocumentManifest` was trial-use/FMM 2, and the R6 package removes the StructureDefinition while marking the name only in `fhir-old-types`. The local inputs do not include the official rationale, so the necessity of the removal cannot be proven. Still, the real less-breaking base alternative would materially undercut the cleanup by preserving the old resource identity and operational surface in R6 core, so the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best backward-compatible base design would have kept the same `resourceType: DocumentManifest` and R4 element shape as a deprecated or retired R6 resource, with clearer text discouraging new use. That is a true base-design alternative; a StructureMap, conversion utility, external profile, or extension-only backport would only mitigate migration and would not make R4 instances valid R6 base instances. The alternative is only partial because it keeps validators, parsers, generated classes, REST endpoints, capability metadata, and references alive for a resource R6 appears to have retired, and it risks old and new document/list representations coexisting indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances and generated/API surfaces, but keeps a retired document-manifest resource in core, duplicates collection/document modeling channels, and may require indefinite validator and endpoint support.

evidence.detail: R4 defines a concrete resource type `DocumentManifest` derived from DomainResource.
No R6 package-index entry exists for `StructureDefinition-DocumentManifest.json`, id `DocumentManifest`, or canonical `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/DocumentManifest`.
R6 lists `DocumentManifest` in the old-types CodeSystem.
evidence.quote: An old resource name no longer used in this version of FHIR (deleted or renamed).

evidence.detail: The R6 all-FHIR-types CodeSystem inspected locally does not contain a `DocumentManifest` concept.

examples.examplesMd: The example is intentionally minimal: it includes the R4 required `status` and `content` fields. It is illustrative of the resource-type break; a strict R6 validator will fail before any element-level validation because `DocumentManifest` is not an R6 resource type.

findings.narrativeMd: `DocumentManifest` itself was removed from the R6 core package. This is more severe than a field rename: any existing R4 payload, generated class, REST endpoint, search client, or reference target that depends on the resource name has no direct R6 counterpart. The old-type terminology marker helps identify the legacy name, but it does not make instances valid R6 resources.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `DocumentManifest` can become immediately R6-invalid because the top-level resource type is unknown. This affects validation, parsing, JSON/XML schema generation, generated model classes, resource-type enums, RESTful routing, and reference-type checks. There is no R6 `DocumentManifest` content to map back to R4, so R6-to-R4 representability is not the relevant direction for this finding.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory stored resources, references, subscriptions, search clients, and API routes that mention `DocumentManifest`. Decide whether each manifest should become a `List`, a set of `DocumentReference` resources, a `Composition` in a document `Bundle`, a custom profile/extension, or a non-FHIR archive record. Test both payload validation and operational behavior such as reads, searches, reference resolution, and capability statements.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The break could have been softened by retaining a deprecated resource definition or by publishing an official compatibility map. Because no such definition is present in the R6 core package, compatibility must be handled by migration tooling or profiles outside the base artifact.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The removal is high-confidence. The exact intended replacement is not established by the local computable artifacts, so migration guidance should not be treated as an official crosswalk.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 defines `DocumentManifest` as a concrete resource type, while the R6 ballot package has no `DocumentManifest` StructureDefinition and lists the name only in the old-types code system. That is a real top-level compatibility break: R4 instances with `resourceType: "DocumentManifest"`, generated model classes, REST routes, resource-type enums, and references to `DocumentManifest/{id}` do not have a base R6 resource identity. The break is still probably proportionate because the R4 artifact is trial-use/FMM 2 and the only true base-compatible alternative is to keep a deprecated resource with its operational surface alive, which would preserve duplicate document-collection modeling in core.
keyEvidence: R6 package .index.json has no StructureDefinition entry for DocumentManifest.
R6 CodeSystem-fhir-old-types contains DocumentManifest; R6 CodeSystem-fhir-types does not.
R4 maturity map and StructureDefinition extensions report FMM 2 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral rather than a strong stability promise. It does not erase the hard resource-type break, but it makes retiring the resource more acceptable than it would be for mature or normative content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: an R4-valid top-level DocumentManifest has no R6 base StructureDefinition, and implementations that expose DocumentManifest endpoints, generated classes, resource-type switches, or reference target checks must redesign.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could retain DocumentManifest as a deprecated or retired R6 resource for one transition release. That would preserve most R4 instances and APIs, but it is not low-cost: it keeps validators, generated models, REST/search surfaces, references, and overlapping document/list representations in the base specification. Migration maps or external profiles help implementers but are not base-compatible alternatives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact hard-break assessment and with treating the base-compatible alternative as only partial rather than clearly available; the fresh judgment frames the removal as breaking but probably OK because FMM 2 lowers the stability burden and the compatibility-preserving alternative has material tradeoffs.

findings.title: No inspected R6 resource provides a lossless one-to-one replacement for manifest grouping and metadata

oldState.summary: R4 DocumentManifest groups one or more resource references with manifest-level metadata.

semanticText.definition: The list of Resources that consist of the parts of this manifest.
semanticText.comment: When used for XDS the intended focus of the DocumentManifest is for the reference to target to be a set of DocumentReference Resources. The reference is to Any to support EN 13606 usage, where an extract is DocumentManifest that references List and Composition resources.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `DocumentManifest.content` is required and can reference any FHIR resource. The resource also carries manifest-level identifiers, status, type, subject, creation time, authors, intended recipients, source URI, description, and related identifiers/resources.

newState.summary: R6 has candidate resources with partial overlap but no direct DocumentManifest replacement in the inspected core artifacts.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `List` can group resource references but has its own required `mode`, different lifecycle semantics, and no direct fields for every manifest concept. `DocumentReference` describes a document and its content rather than a manifest of multiple arbitrary resources. `Composition` plus `Bundle` models a FHIR document package, not a general manifest resource.

facts.note: No direct R6 replacement StructureDefinition or ConceptMap was found in local inputs.

facts.newValue: List.entry.item 1..1 Reference(Resource) within repeating List.entry, with List.mode required
facts.note: Structurally similar for grouping, but semantics and required fields differ.

facts.oldValue: manifest contains references to resources, often DocumentReference resources
facts.newValue: DocumentReference.content describes the referenced document and alternate formats/metadata
facts.note: Not a manifest of multiple independent resources.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The candidate resources were identified by local semantic overlap, not by an official rename. `List`, `DocumentReference`, `Composition`, and `Bundle` each cover a different document or collection pattern, so a migration rule must be chosen from implementation context.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This finding is about conversion semantics after accepting that the original resource type is removed. A migration can usually create some R6 representation, but the transform is not mechanically lossless: choices such as `List.mode`, mapping `superseded` status, preserving recipients and source URI, and representing manifest-level related identifiers may require extensions or local policy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect mapping can change what a document collection means, who it was intended for, or how related orders/workflows are traced. That is mainly an interoperability and records-management risk, with possible clinical workflow impact in document-exchange deployments.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate document and collection modeling into existing R6 resources rather than carrying a separate manifest resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the deprecated DocumentManifest resource as the base compatibility carrier for manifest grouping and metadata; mapping guidance alone is migration support, not base compatibility.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Once `DocumentManifest` is removed, its required `content` list and manifest-level metadata have no inspected one-to-one R6 carrier. Consolidating these use cases into existing R6 document and collection resources is a plausible goal because `List`, `DocumentReference`, and document Bundles each cover more specific patterns. A less-breaking base design exists only by retaining the old resource content model; ConceptMaps, StructureMaps, profiles, and extensions can reduce migration divergence but do not preserve R4 instance validity in the R6 base model. Because retaining the old carrier creates material duplication and interoperability costs, the break is probably justified on the local evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base alternative would keep `DocumentManifest.content`, `status`, `type`, `subject`, `created`, `author`, `recipient`, `source`, `description`, and `related` inside a deprecated R6 `DocumentManifest` resource, then document optional mappings to `List.entry.item`, `List.code`, `List.date`, `List.source`, `DocumentReference`, or `Composition`/`Bundle` where appropriate. This would preserve most R4-valid instances better than an external map. It remains partial because the same manifest facts could then be represented either in the legacy resource or in newer R6 patterns, with validation ambiguity, synchronization risk, and long-term accumulation of deprecated representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids most field-level data loss, but preserves overlapping same-domain representations and leaves ambiguous source-of-truth choices between DocumentManifest, List, DocumentReference, Composition, and Bundle.

evidence.detail: R4 requires `DocumentManifest.content` as `1..* Reference(Resource)` and describes it as the list of resources that are parts of the manifest.
evidence.quote: The list of Resources that consist of the parts of this manifest.

evidence.detail: R4 explicitly allowed both XDS-style sets of DocumentReference resources and broader EN 13606 usages involving List and Composition resources.
R6 List has a repeating entry backbone with required `entry.item` Reference(Resource), but List also has required lifecycle fields and list-specific semantics.
evidence.quote: A List is a curated collection of resources

evidence.detail: R6 DocumentReference content represents the referenced document and formats, not a manifest list of arbitrary resources.
evidence.quote: If there are multiple content element repetitions, these must all represent the same document in different format, or attachment metadata.

evidence.detail: No R6 StructureDefinition named `DocumentManifest` was found to provide a same-artifact target for the R4 content model.

examples.examplesMd: This is an illustrative candidate transform, not an official map. It must invent or choose `List.mode`, and it does not show how to preserve every R4 manifest field such as `recipient`, `source` URI, or `related.identifier`.

findings.narrativeMd: Because the R6 artifact is absent, the practical migration question is whether the R4 manifest's collection semantics can be preserved elsewhere. The inspected R6 candidates are not simple renames. A `List` can hold entries, but it carries list-specific processing mode and status semantics; a `DocumentReference` points to one document; a `Composition`/`Bundle` document has a different packaging model. Implementers therefore face semantic migration work, not just field renaming.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an additional old-valid/new-invalid rule beyond the removed resource. Instead, it affects compatibility of transformed data: a syntactically valid R6 `List` or `DocumentReference` may still fail to preserve the R4 manifest's intended recipients, source system URI, related identifiers, or distinction between a manifest and the documents it lists. Generated converters cannot safely infer all choices without profile or workflow knowledge.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before converting, classify each R4 manifest by use case. For simple curated collections of resource references, consider an R6 `List` with a documented policy for `mode`, status mapping, identifiers, subject, date, and source. For actual document packages, assess `Composition` in a document `Bundle`. For XDS-style references, preserve or create `DocumentReference` resources and use a separate grouping mechanism. Preserve unmapped manifest metadata with extensions only after defining governance and round-trip expectations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative would have been an official migration map plus extensions for fields without direct targets. This would not fully avoid semantic change because the possible target models emphasize different concepts, but it would reduce inconsistent local mappings and lower the cost of validating migrated instances.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Requires human review because the right target is deployment-specific and no official R6 ballot4 mapping was available in the local inputs.

freshReview.narrativeMd: At the affected path, R4 `DocumentManifest.content` is a required repeating `Reference(Resource)` list of the manifest parts. R6 has no same resource or same path. `List.entry.item` and `Composition.section.entry` can carry resource references, while `DocumentReference.content` represents formats or metadata for one document rather than a manifest of independent resources. A converter therefore needs workflow-specific choices, especially for whether the R4 manifest should become a List, a document Bundle/Composition pattern, or another local representation. That is real semantic migration work, but it is largely a consequence of retiring the trial-use resource and does not show a separate low-cost base design beyond retaining the old resource.
keyEvidence: R4 DocumentManifest.content: min=1, max=*, type=Reference(Resource), definition is the list of resources that are parts of the manifest.
R4 DocumentManifest.content comment cites XDS-style sets of DocumentReference resources and EN 13606 usage with List and Composition resources.
R6 List.entry.item is Reference(Resource), but List also has required status and mode with list-specific semantics.
R6 DocumentReference.content is about the referenced document and alternate formats/attachment metadata, not a multi-resource manifest.
A local R6 package search found DocumentManifest only in CodeSystem-fhir-old-types, not in a mapping or replacement StructureDefinition.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use keeps the stability concern moderate. The required content list is central to the old resource, but the artifact maturity does not by itself justify carrying the old content model indefinitely.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation with conversion loss risk: this is not an additional structural validation break separate from the removed resource, but transformed R6 data can lose the intended grouping semantics or require local policy to choose List, Composition/Bundle, DocumentReference grouping, status, mode, and metadata mappings.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: For this path alone, the only strong base-compatible alternative is to keep a deprecated DocumentManifest resource with its `content` element. An official map or recommended profile could reduce inconsistent migration, but it would not make R4 instances valid R6 base instances. Keeping the old content model would preserve semantics but duplicate R6 collection/document patterns and create long-term ambiguity about the preferred carrier.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium-impact, no-direct-model assessment. The fresh path-level review agrees that migration is not lossless, but it treats the finding as a semantic conversion burden after the resource removal rather than an independent hard break, and it views the less-breaking option as only partial.

Because the R6 artifact is absent, there is no same-path R6 binding to compare; status code-system contents inspected locally were unchanged for the directly reused document-reference-status code system.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 retains DocumentManifest only as an old-type marker
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The marker itself is not a breaking model change; the break is the absence of the resource definition. The CodeSystem entry is useful evidence and may help tooling recognize legacy names, but it does not make `DocumentManifest` a valid R6 resource.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validators and conversion tooling can use the old-type marker to produce clearer diagnostics or to trigger a migration workflow for legacy `DocumentManifest` payloads.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `List` is the closest generic R6 resource for a curated collection of resource references, but it has its own required `mode`, status semantics, and entry model. Analyze its R4-to-R6 changes before using it as a migration target.

R4 DocumentManifest comments identify XDS-style manifests of DocumentReference resources as an intended use. R6 DocumentReference should be analyzed separately because it may hold the document-level metadata while another resource groups references.
For document-package use cases, R6 Composition-in-Bundle may be a better target than List, but it has different document semantics and constraints that need separate assessment.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot narrative, or committee change note for `DocumentManifest` was available in the local inputs. The `fhir-old-types` CodeSystem is strong evidence of intentional removal but does not explain rationale or intended replacement.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official R6 ballot narrative/change history or tracker items for DocumentManifest removal.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official cross-version ConceptMap or StructureMap was found for converting R4 DocumentManifest instances into an R6 representation. Migration guidance is therefore based on structural and semantic overlap with related resources, not an authoritative map.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Provide an official or implementation-guide-specific conversion map, including handling for `recipient`, `source`, `related`, and status semantics.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology was not expanded through a terminology server. Direct CodeSystem inspection was sufficient for the removal finding and status-code spot check, but expansion-based comparison could reveal subtler changes in candidate target bindings.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansions for bindings used in candidate migration targets and compare them with R4 bindings used by DocumentManifest.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build package marked not-for-publication. The removal is valid for this local package, but future ballot/publication changes could reintroduce or further clarify the artifact.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the analysis against the final R6 publication package or a later ballot build.
